references.text: The immediate context describing how the children of Israel broke camp and set up their tents according to the movements of the cloud over the tabernacle.
Explains the principle that the Israelites remained in camp as long as the cloud rested over the tabernacle, whether for two days, a month, or longer.
Describes how the cloud over the tabernacle guided Israel's journeys: when the cloud lifted, they broke camp; when it did not lift, they waited.
The Levites were to keep watch at the Lord's tabernacle, using a similar expression for keeping the Lord's charge (mishméret).
Describes the Levites' service of keeping watch for Aaron and the entire congregation at the tent of meeting.
An exhortation to keep the Lord's charges (mishméret), corresponding to the Israelites' obedience in keeping the Lord's watch.
A poetic description of how God spread out a cloud as a covering, referring to the cloud's guidance of Israel.
